Title: Technical Director (video world models; founder of Morpheus AI, acquired by Roblox)
Use case: Serve Super Upsampler video world model at the edge
Why now: Roblox Reality (Apr 2026) runs an AI model (Super Upsampler) for every player at the edge on H200/B200-class GPUs; Roblox says it does not yet run in real time and that its high compute cost is a challenge to solve. In Jun 2026 it acquired Morpheus AI, whose founder invented Self Forcing for fast interactive video models.

Title: Co-Founder
Segment: AI-native game studio / generative game engine
Use case: Serve Reverie real-time diffusion render layer
Why now: Opened the beta of its world modeling agent and Generative Game Engine in Feb 2026 to a 10,000+ waitlist. Its Reverie diffusion model is built to run as a low-latency layer of the game engine, where about 100 ms of delay breaks immersion.

Title: CEO
Use case: Serve playable generative video at scale
Why now: Raised a $5M pre-seed in Nov 2026 (Play Ventures, Backed VC, Supercell) for generative video that responds to player input in real time, with a creator platform planned for early 2027. It is building its own inference tech to make generative video faster and cheaper, a build-vs-buy decision Reactor can win.

Title: Founder & CEO
Use case: Real-time multimedia story frames for Emochi
Why now: Closed a roughly $60M round in Jul 2026; Emochi has 2M+ daily users and about $45M ARR. Kaon runs 1,000+ GPUs across Nebius and DigitalOcean and its CEO says it is moving toward real-time multimedia narratives.

Title: Co-Founder, Head of Machine Learning
Use case: Serve fine-tuned behavior models under tight latency
Why now: Per a May 2026 AWS case study, Artificial Agency is fine-tuning Llama models at 1B, 3B and 8B for always-on gameplay under strict latency budgets, aiming to run in real time across millions of concurrent players. Its Behavior Engine powers NPCs in a single-player mode of Owlchemy Labs' XR game Dimensional Double Shift. Its models are text and behavior, not video, so fit is serving its own checkpoints.

Title: CEO
Use case: Serve Roll-01 world model for playable video
Why now: A Feb 2026 release describes Yoroll.ai as an engine-less game platform that uses generative video as its primary rendering layer, running Google Genie 3 or LinearGame's own Roll-01 model, with a vision-language model that detects events in the video stream in real time. LinearGame raised a multi-million-dollar pre-seed (reported Dec 2025) to launch Yoroll.ai for short-form video creators.

Title: AI Character Visual & Technology Leader
Use case: Real-time AI character video rendering
Why now: Founded by miHoYo co-founder Cai Haoyu; its Steam title Whispers from the Star uses LLMs and multimodal AI to render scenes and dialogue in real time, with players talking to the character by text, voice or video. In Aug 2026 it was reported to be developing a next-generation game-specific model capable of emotional understanding and autonomous interaction.

Title: Chief AI Officer (CAIO)
Use case: Serve in-house world models for games and sim
Why now: In Oct 2026 Krafton and Seoul National University launched a three-year joint research center (CAIO Kangwook Lee attended) whose projects include keeping spaces and objects consistent in long AI-generated videos. On its Jul 2026 call the CEO said Krafton is seeking outside investment alongside its own AI spending and that game data is a strength in world model development.

Title: Founder
Use case: Serve proprietary per-player world generation models
Why now: Raised a strategic round led by SeaX Ventures and Pix Capital in Jun 2026 for Tomo: Endless Blue, an open-world RPG that uses proprietary AI models to create settlements, NPCs, conversations and missions for each player. The game targets a late 2026 PC (Steam) release, so inference serving at launch is a near-term need.

Title: Founder & CEO
Segment: AI-native game studio / generative game engine
Use case: Serve own spatial model for live world generation
Why now: Raised a $4.49M seed in Nov 2026 to build a multimodal spatial-reasoning model that turns text or image prompts into controllable 3D scenes, assets and NPCs, alongside its AI-native PC game EchoShell and its self-built Creation Engine for developers.

Title: VP, AI Programs
Use case: Low-latency serving for player-facing gen AI
Why now: In its full-year results Ubisoft said it is accelerating investment behind Teammates, its first playable generative AI experience (revealed Nov 2025), a shooter where players direct AI squadmates by voice. Ubisoft says these AI systems can react more dynamically in real time.

Title: Senior Director, AI Platform & Infrastructure
Use case: Low-latency runtime AI serving for UEFN creators
Why now: In Apr 2026 Epic released Fortnite Conversations (AI NPCs using Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite plus ElevenLabs) as an Experimental feature for creators, saying LLM response times are slower than it expects for the final release. Epic said in Jun 2026 that UE6 will let studios bring their own favorite models.

Title: Chief Strategy Officer
Use case: Real-time generative layer for living game worlds
Why now: At Runway's AI Summit (Aug 2026) EA's CSO said AI in games has to run "60 times per second, endlessly, for many, many, many hours," in sync across thousands of people playing together, and described existing game systems as deterministic, reliable and controllable. EA is also exploring AI systems with Stability AI that pre-visualize 3D environments from prompts.

Title: CEO & Co-Founder
Use case: Serve generated scene video for Voyage RPG worlds
Why now: Launched Voyage in Apr 2026, an AI RPG platform built on its own World Engine that combines proprietary models with Gemini Flash for images and Gemma for text, audio and video, with an open beta planned later in 2026. Adding generated video per player would raise serving latency and cost.

Title: Co-Founder & CEO
Use case: Real-time world-model game types for UGC creators
Why now: Raised $56M (Series A led by Sea, Series B led by Sequoia, NVIDIA participating) in May 2026, claiming 20M+ users and hundreds of millions of monthly plays. Agentic game creation at that volume is a natural place to add playable world-model formats.

Title: Technical Director
Use case: Serve Glossa game model and AI characters at scale
Why now: In May 2026 miHoYo said it will invest up to RMB 100B (about $14.7B) in AI over three years, building an internal ecosystem with training systems and GPU clusters, with the tech to be used for NPCs in Petit Planet. It has been developing Glossa, its own game-specific large model.

Title: President of Games
Use case: Generated interactive TV experiences over cloud
Why now: Netflix said in Jan 2026 it will continue to invest in its cloud-first gaming strategy and expects its cloud games catalog to expand further in 2026. In Jul 2026 it said generative AI was used in roughly 300 of its titles in 2026, so it already has gen AI production pipelines for shows and films.

Title: Founder
Use case: Runtime serving for AI NPCs and world reactivity
Why now: Raised $8.5M (Transcend-led, with Bitkraft participating) for SolidRiver, a survival city-builder that uses AI for NPC behavior and world reactivity, and is building AI tech that could be licensed to other studios (Naavik, Jun 2026). It is hiring Unreal Engine developers.

Title: Co-Founder & CEO
Use case: Faster runtime generation for in-game heroes and scenarios
Why now: YOU vs. Zombies launched in summer 2026 with "The Ritual," a custom AI generation system that turns anyone or anything into a playable hero; the CEO says scenario generation now takes about 13 seconds, down from at least a minute. It uses Gemini plus image models such as Z-Image and partners like fal.ai.

Title: AI Project Manager
Use case: Low-latency multimodal companion in a live MMO
Why now: Square Enix is adding Chatty Slimey, a Gemini-powered companion that analyzes information from the game screen and generates voiced conversation, to the live MMO Dragon Quest X (beta test applications closed Mar 30, 2026). Google describes it as a real-time, multimodal companion.
